Bioinformatics has more than one job. Start with the biological question, then identify the data you need. Do you need to code before you can analyse biological data? A GUI gives you visual controls. A CLI accepts typed commands. Both can support serious work. You have sequencing reads. Do you place them on a map or build the map?

Reads can be used in different ways. Reference alignment estimates where reads fit against an existing sequence. De novo assembly reconstructs longer sequences from relationships among reads without using a reference as the primary template. These approaches can be combined: reads can be aligned back to an assembly for evaluation. The right route depends on your question, reference suitability and data quality. Save the two-route guide.

A file extension is a clue to what you can do next. FASTA holds sequences; FASTQ adds per-base quality information.
